column2: ENGLISH

For six hundred years the Empire has had no crowned Emperor, only rival claimants and the Electors who will not choose between them. Now the nobles speak your name in their halls, and the priests speak it from their pulpits. Your renown and your piety are known from the Reik to the Talabec. If you proclaim your claim, the Electors will have to answer it.
Proclaim it from every temple!
Not yet.
In a week you are crowned §YEmperor§!, and the §YHammer of Sigmar§! is yours, from whoever holds it now. A month later every independent Elector of the Empire must kneel to you or refuse.

The Grand Theogonist sets the crown upon your head before the high altar, and the cathedral rings with the hymns of Sigmar. Then he places in your hands Ghal Maraz, the Skull-Splitter, the hammer Sigmar himself carried, given to him by Kurgan Ironbeard of the Dawi. Outside, the bells of every temple in the city are ringing. Word goes out to the Electors: the Empire has an Emperor again.
For Sigmar and the Empire!

A herald stands in your hall with a letter under the seal of [From.GetTitledFirstName]. [From.GetSheHeCap] has been crowned [From.GetTitle], [From.GetSheHe] writes, by the will of the people and the blessing of the cults, and the division of the Empire is at an end. [From.GetSheHeCap] asks you to kneel and take your place among [From.GetHerHis] Electors.
Let the division end. I will kneel.
Never. I will not bend the knee to this usurper!
You put aside any rival Imperial crown, and your realm joins the §YEmpire§!.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] kneels before your throne and lays [From.GetHerHis] sword at your feet.\n\n"My liege, I ask you to forgive my part in the troubles. May a new age of unity and glory begin under your rule."
Well said. Rise, my Elector.
You have refused the false Emperor before your whole court. Not all your vassals were pleased to hear it. The softer-hearted among them say you have put your own crown before the Empire.
Bah, let them grumble!
[From.GetTitledFirstName] sends your herald back with a single answer:\n\n"I would rather see the Empire fall to ruin than kneel to you. I shall see you on the battlefield, usurper."
Traitor! The Electors' crowns are mine by right.
One Faith Triumphant

For more than six hundred years the great cults have backed rival thrones. In 1359 IC Ottilia of Talabecland named Sigmar a false god and crowned herself Empress, and every cult has had a claimant of its own ever since.\n\nWith the crown on the head of [Root.GetTitledFirstName] the feud is over. The Grand Theogonist stands first among the priests of the Empire, as he did in the days of the heirs of Sigmar, and the bells of the Great Cathedral ring from Altdorf to the Middle Mountains. Ar-Ulric and the High Priest of Taal keep their temples and their flocks, and their priests sit again beside the priests of Sigmar at the Emperor's council. The faithful of every cult may marry one another, and the old curses are struck from the pulpits.

For more than six hundred years the great cults have backed rival thrones. In 1359 IC Ottilia of Talabecland named Sigmar a false god and crowned herself Empress, and every cult has had a claimant of its own ever since.\n\nWith the crown on the head of [Root.GetTitledFirstName] the feud is over, and it is the White Wolf who howls loudest. Ulric was the god of the tribes long before Sigmar walked among them, and now his cult stands first among the cults of the Empire again. The eternal flame of Middenheim burns before the Emperor's throne. The Grand Theogonist keeps his cathedral and his flock, but it is the word of Ar-Ulric that is heard at court. The faithful of every cult may marry one another, and the old curses are struck from the pulpits.

For more than six hundred years the great cults have backed rival thrones. In 1359 IC Ottilia of Talabecland named Sigmar a false god and crowned herself Empress, and every cult has had a claimant of its own ever since.\n\nWith the crown on the head of [Root.GetTitledFirstName] the feud is over, and the Lord of the Wild has the Emperor's ear. The Cult of Taal and Rhya stands first among the cults of the Empire, and antlered priests of Taal walk the halls of the palace with mud on their feet. The Grand Theogonist and Ar-Ulric keep their temples and their flocks. The faithful of every cult may marry one another, and the old curses are struck from the pulpits.
One Empire, under all its gods.

The schism of the cults is ended. The faithful of Sigmar, Ulric, Taal, Morr and Manann may marry one another, and the triumphant cult gains authority. The other cults keep their temples and their faithful.
Crowned by the head of a great cult, you gain a §Ystrong claim§! on the §YEmpire§!, which halves the price of claiming the throne.
Call in the Runefangs

Alaric the Mad forged twelve Runefangs for the twelve chieftains who followed Sigmar, one for each Elector of the Empire. Command that every sword be brought to the rightful holder of its Elector crown. The swords of crowns with no worthy holder will hang in your own hall until one is found.
§YGhal Maraz§! comes back to you, and every §YRunefang§! goes to the worthy holder of its Elector crown, taken from whoever has it now. You keep the swords of crowns with no worthy holder.
You have not called in the Runefangs in the last five years
The Peace of the Cults

Since 1359 IC the cults of Sigmar, Ulric and Taal have fought for mastery of the Empire, each with a claimant of its own. The Vampire Wars have humbled them all. If they do not stand together now, the dead will take what is left. The Grand Theogonist has called for peace among the cults, and their faithful may marry one another again.

Since 1359 IC the cults of Sigmar, Ulric and Taal have fought for mastery of the Empire, each with a claimant of its own. Now a Black Crusade marches out of the north, and the Empire must stand together or burn. The Grand Theogonist has called for peace among the cults, and their faithful may marry one another again.

Since 1359 IC the cults of Sigmar, Ulric and Taal have fought for mastery of the Empire, each with a claimant of its own. The Grand Theogonist has called for peace among them, and their faithful may marry one another again. Not every priest is pleased. Some say the peace is a surrender.
Let there be peace among the faithful.
We must stop this threat at any cost. Send envoys to our rivals and the Dawi.
We must stop this threat at any cost. Plead with Bretonnia.
There will be no peace with heretics.
Trouble in the Empire

An envoy of [From.GetTitledFirstName] has come to your court. The dead are on the march in the Empire, the envoy says, and if the Imperial lines break they will not stop at its borders. [From.GetSheHeCap] asks for an alliance. Your advisors urge you to accept, before the war comes to you.

An envoy of [From.GetTitledFirstName], your rival for the Imperial throne, has come to your court asking for an alliance against the undead that threaten you both. Your advisors remind you that if you win the war together, the rivalry will go on after it. Perhaps it would be wiser to let [From.GetHerHim] fend for [From.GetHerselfHimself].

An envoy of [From.GetTitledFirstName] has come to your court. A Black Crusade marches on the Empire, the envoy says, and if the Empire falls the hordes will not stop at its borders. [From.GetSheHeCap] asks for an alliance against the Ruinous Powers.
I accept this treaty.
I shall decline.
The Imperial Throne

In 1979 IC the Grand Theogonist of Sigmar refused to crown Magritta of Marienburg, though the Electors had chosen her. It ended the election of Emperors and threw the Empire into strife. [This.GetTitledFirstName] means to right that wrong and press [This.GetHerHis] claim, but reports are coming in of dark rituals in Sylvania.

In 1979 IC the Grand Theogonist of Sigmar rightly refused to crown Magritta of Marienburg Empress. It ended the election of Emperors and threw the Empire into strife. [This.GetTitledFirstName] means to press [This.GetHerHis] own claim to the throne, but reports are coming in of dark rituals in Sylvania.
The Empire is mine, by right.
The vampire threat comes first.

One hundred Knights Panther kneel before the throne, the most loyal men of the Order, and rise as Templars of Sigmar. They will guard the Temple of Sigmar and the Emperor's own city, and their drill is to be the strictest in the Empire. They call themselves the Knights Griffon, and [griffon_grandmaster.GetTitledFirstName] is their first Grand Master.
Guard His temple well.
Riders bring word from [From.GetTitledFirstName]. The Emperor has raised a new order of Templars from the finest Knights Panther, the Knights Griffon, sworn to guard the Temple of Sigmar.
Sigmar protects.
Found the Knights Griffon
Magnus the Pious raised the Knights Griffon from the most loyal Knights Panther at his court. With the Empire whole again under Sigmar, I can found this order of Templars to guard His temple.
The Knights Griffon are founded, led by a Grand Master drawn from the Knights Panther.
Expelled the Knights Griffon
Expelled the Horned Hunters
Renew Ottilia's Edict

In 1360 Ottilia of Talabecland named Sigmar a false god and outlawed his cult. The Edict has been dead letter for generations, but the old proclamation still lies in the archives. Renew it, and the priests of the Hammer will be outlawed in your lands once more.
Revoke Ottilia's Edict
End the Edict against the cult of Sigmar. The priests of the Hammer may preach again, and the Sigmarite lords will have no cause to rise.
§YOttilia's Edict§! is proclaimed: the cult of Sigmar is outlawed in your realm. Your Sigmarite vassals must turn to your faith or refuse, and those who refuse may rise against you in a year.
§YOttilia's Edict§! ends. The cult of Sigmar may preach freely again.

The clerk sets the old parchment before me. Its seal is the wolf of Ulric beside the arms of Talabecland, and its words are as hard as the day Ottilia wrote them: Sigmar was a man, a great man, but a man, and no god. His priests have grown fat on the tithes of the Empire, and they have crowned and uncrowned Emperors as it pleased them.\n\nIf I renew the Edict, the Hammer's temples in my lands will close. The question is how loudly I wish to say it.
Burn their temples. Let the smoke carry the message.
The Sigmarite temples of §YAltdorf§! (or another Sigmarite city of your realm) are put to the torch.
Outlaw the cult. The temples may stand empty.
Not yet. The time is not right.
Ottilia's Edict

Heralds ride out with the proclamation of [From.GetTitledFirstName]: the Edict of Ottilia is renewed. Sigmar is named a false god in [From.GetHerHis] lands, his priests are outlawed, and every lord who keeps the Hammer must turn from it or answer for it.

The sky over the city glowed red for three nights. On the orders of [From.GetTitledFirstName] the temples of Sigmar were put to the torch, the priests dragged into the streets and the relics thrown into the flames. Ottilia's Edict is renewed: Sigmar is named a false god, and his faithful must turn or answer for it.
Sigmar will not forget this.
At last, the old truth is spoken again.
The men of the Empire quarrel over their gods again.

A herald of [From.GetTitledFirstName] reads the Edict in my hall before my household and my priests. The cult of Sigmar is outlawed. I am to turn to [From.Religion.GetName] and pull down the Hammer from my chapel, or be named an enemy of my liege.
I will turn. Sigmar was only a man.
I will turn... in public.
Never. I will not deny the Heldenhammer.

A year has passed under the Edict. Today a wandering priest of Sigmar stood on the steps of my own hall with a hammer in his hand and a crowd at his back, and named me a tyrant and a heretic before them all. My guards hold him now. The Sigmarite lords who refused the Edict are watching what I do next.
Burn him. Let the faithful of the Hammer see it.
Drive him from my lands.
Let him preach. Words break no walls.

The Sigmarite lords who refused the Edict of [From.GetTitledFirstName] have raised their banners. They march under the Hammer and the twin-tailed comet, sworn to see the Edict torn down. The War of the Hammer has begun.
Sigmar guide their swords.
Brother against brother, as ever.
The Edict Ends
Ottilia's Edict is no more. The doors of the Sigmarite temples open again, the priests return to their pulpits, and the faithful of the Hammer give thanks that the long night is over. For now.

The faithful of Sigmar have won. Under the Hammer and the comet they broke my armies and forced the Edict from my hand. The temples open again, and the priests of the Hammer sing in the streets as though they had crowned an Emperor themselves.
So be it.
With the title comes the Edict of Ottilia, still in force. The priests of my faith expect me to keep it. The Sigmarite lords expect me to let it lapse, and some of them will rise if I do not.
The Edict stands.
Let it lapse. I need peace more than I need old quarrels.
I keep no faith of the Wolf or the Huntsman. The Edict ends with my predecessor.
Word comes that Ottilia's Edict is ended. The cult of Sigmar may preach freely again, and the Hammer hangs once more above the altars where it was pulled down.
Praise the Heldenhammer.
Until the next Emperor tears it up again.

The rebels of the Hammer are broken. My priests urge me to mark the victory with a great temple in [Root.Capital.GetName], not to one god, but to the gods of the Old World that the Empire honoured before Sigmar was ever named among them. The masons await my word on whom it shall honour.
Ulric and Taal, the elder brothers.
The gods of war: Ulric and Myrmidia.
The gods of plenty: Rhya, Shallya and Handrich.
The watchers: Morr and Verena.
There is no coin for temples.
War of the Hammer
$FIRST_ADJ$ War of the Hammer
The Sigmarite lords who refused Ottilia's Edict rise against their liege. Victory ends the Edict.
Outlawed Sigmar
Turned at the Edict
Burned a Priest of Sigmar
Spared a Priest of Sigmar
Sigmar Outlawed
Ottilia's Edict
The Hammer Restored
Temples of Sigmar Burned
The temples of Sigmar in this city were put to the torch under Ottilia's Edict. The ashes still smoulder, and so does the anger of the faithful.
Pantheon of the Elder Brothers
A great temple to Ulric and Taal, the elder brothers among the gods of the Old World. Wolf pelts and stag antlers hang from its rafters.
Pantheon of the Gods of War
A great temple to Ulric and Myrmidia, where captains swear their oaths before battle.
Pantheon of Plenty
A great temple to Rhya, Shallya and Handrich. Its granaries feed the poor and its counting-house the treasury.
Pantheon of the Watchers
A great temple to Morr and Verena, with a garden of ravens and a library of sealed books.
ENGLISH

[university_student.GetTitledFirstName] stands before you, cap in hand, and asks leave to go to the [university.GetName]. [university_student.GetSheHeCap] wants to read law and history and the natural philosophers, to hear the great masters dispute, and to come home a learned [university_student.GetManWoman]. The masters' fees are not small, and students are known to learn a great deal besides their books.
Go, and make me proud.
I will not allow it!

You have decided to send [university_student.GetTitledFirstName] to a university, in the hope that [university_student.GetSheHe] comes home a learned [university_student.GetManWoman]. Where will you send [university_student.GetHerHim]?
To the University of Altdorf.
To the University of Nuln.
To the University of Streissen.
To the University of Praag.
To the University of Remas.
To the University of Miragliano.
To the University of Martek.
To the University of Magritta.
On second thoughts, no. [university_student.GetFirstName] stays.
Away at University
This character is studying at a university and will come home in a few years.

[university_student.GetTitledFirstName] is home from the [university.GetName], and one look is enough. [university_student.GetSheHeCap] smells of the tavern, laughs too loud and calls for wine before noon. It makes you wonder how [university_student.GetSheHe] ever passed an examination.
Damn sot.

[university_student.GetTitledFirstName] is home from the [university.GetName], and changed. [university_student.GetSheHeCap] is wiser, surer of [university_student.GetHerHis] own mind, and full of things you never knew. The masters taught [university_student.GetHerHim] well.
Welcome home, [university_student.GetFirstName]!

[university_student.GetTitledFirstName] is home from the [university.GetName] with [university_student.GetHerHis] studies finished, but they have taken a great deal out of [university_student.GetHerHim]. Too many sleepless nights over the books have left [university_student.GetHerHim] grey and joyless.
It cannot have been that hard.

[university_student.GetTitledFirstName] is home from the [university.GetName], and not alone. [university_student.GetSheHeCap] has found a spouse among the students' lodgings and brought [university_student.GetHerHis] new family home to meet you.
Each to their own.

[university_student.GetTitledFirstName] is home from the [university.GetName], dragging [university_student.GetHerHis] feet. The cities are full of fevers and the students' lodgings are full of the cities' worst. [university_student.GetSheHeCap] will need to rest a long while.
Poor child.

[university_student.GetTitledFirstName] is home from the [university.GetName] with three carts of books behind [university_student.GetHerHim] and a head full of more. [university_student.GetSheHeCap] loved every day of it, and talks of nothing else.
I doubt they will all fit in the library.

[university_student.GetTitledFirstName] is home from the [university.GetName]. Having heard some of [university_student.GetHerHis] stories of wine, dice, duels and the daughters of innkeepers, you decide a student's life must be quite something.
That's my [university_student.GetFirstName]!

[university_student.GetTitledFirstName] has done better than anyone hoped. [university_student.GetSheHeCap] is home from the [university.GetName] a master of the old sorcery of Araby, with the flames of the desert at [university_student.GetHerHis] fingertips. A scholar of such learning will bring great honour to the family.
Excellent.
A Bound Thesis
A thesis written at a university of the Old World and thought worthy of binding by its masters. The margins are full of the author's later corrections.
[university_student.GetFirstName] goes to live at the court of the §YRector§! of the university for four years.

A letter from [From.GetFirstName] in Altdorf:\n\n"The lectures are long and the masters are dull, but the city is never dull. Half the nobility of the Empire sends its children here, to be schooled and to find a good match, and I have dined with the sons of three Electors. From my window I can see the towers of the Colleges of Magic, and at night strange lights burn in them. I am well, but the capital is dear, and my purse grows light."

A letter from [From.GetFirstName] in Nuln:\n\n"The University of Nuln is older than the Empire's oldest crowns, and its masters never let us forget it. There are students here from as far away as Araby. When the Gunnery School tests its guns the whole city shakes and the ink jumps on my desk. I am learning a great deal, but the books alone cost a fortune."

A letter from [From.GetFirstName] in Streissen:\n\n"It is a small university, and the medical school is the best part of it. The town is all whitewashed houses and parks, and it is full of talk that the Averheim bailiffs would not like to hear. The masters who taught such things were turned out years ago, but the students still whisper. Do not worry, I keep my head down. I could keep it down more easily with a little more silver."

A letter from [From.GetFirstName] in Praag:\n\n"They say the stones of this city remember the Great War against Chaos, and some nights I believe it. Faces show in the walls when the lamps go out, and no student walks the old quarter alone. The masters are stern and the winters are worse. I have learned to drink kvas and to sleep with a candle burning. Please send warm clothes, or money for them."

A letter from [From.GetFirstName] in Remas:\n\n"Remas sits on its great headland above the lagoon, and its fishermen are the best in the Old World. The city is a republic, and every student here has an opinion on how a city should be ruled and shouts it in the taverns. The Elves built here before men came, and the masters take us out to measure their ruins. I have learned more law and rhetoric in a year than in all my life before. The city is very dear, and the Tileans charge a foreigner double for everything."

A letter from [From.GetFirstName] in Miragliano:\n\n"Miragliano is built on islands, with canals for streets, and it is a city of engineers. and the masters speak of the great Leonardo as though he left yesterday. I have seen machines here that the Dwarfs would envy. The fevers come up from the Blighted Marshes in summer, so I keep to my rooms and my books. The sea is salt and the rivers are miles away, so the city buys its water by the barrel. Everything costs money here, even the water."

A letter from [From.GetFirstName] in Magritta:\n\n"Every ship of the south seems to come into the Bay of Quietude, even ships from Araby. The great temple of Myrmidia, which all her temples in the Old World obey, rises over the harbour, and the masters here are as fond of the sword as of the pen. I have been taught the diestro way of fencing by a man who fights duels over the placing of a comma. The Estalians are proud and quick to take offence, so I am learning courtesy as well as letters. A gentleman's education here is not cheap."

A letter from [From.GetFirstName] in Martek:\n\n"Martek stands high in the mountains, and vultures big enough to carry off a horse circle its towers. Its scholars study the stars, and they say the fire of the heavens can be read like a book. I have seen one of them call a flame into his hand. The days are hot, the nights are cold and the copying of books never ends. The masters expect gifts from their pupils, as is the custom of Araby."
Send a purse of silver.
[From.GetSheHeCap] must learn to live within [From.GetHerHis] means.
With money to spare, [From.GetFirstName] is more likely to come home §Ybetter educated§!, but also more likely to come home a §Ydrunkard§! or a §Yhedonist§!.
Living on little, [From.GetFirstName] is more likely to come home a §Yscholar§!, but also more likely to come home §Yworn out§!.
Endow the University
Pay for new halls, books and chairs at the university of your city. Its learning will spread through your lands, and its students will come home wiser.
Endowed University
A lord has paid for new halls, books and chairs. Learning spreads faster here, and the students graduate learned more often.

A rider in your family's colours comes into the university courtyard with mud to the knees and a sealed letter. [From.GetName] is yours now, and your people need their lord more than the masters need another pupil. Your books are packed by nightfall.
My studies must wait. I am needed at home.
University of Talabheim
University of Salzenmund
University of Marienburg
To the University of Talabheim.
To the University of Salzenmund.
To the University of Marienburg.
To the University of Kufra.

A letter from [From.GetFirstName] in Talabheim:\n\n"The city lies inside a great crater in the heart of the Great Forest, and from the rim you can see the whole of it, fields and temples and all, walled in by stone that no army has ever climbed. The universities here are for young nobles, and most of my fellows study the wine of the taverns and the ladies of the city more than their books. I try to be the exception. It is not cheap to be the exception."

A letter from [From.GetFirstName] in Salzenmund:\n\n"Salzenmund is a free town and proud of it, and the university is the newest thing in it. The masters of sciences here are bold men who say the world can be understood, and the old priests mutter about them. West of the town lies the Laurelorn, and the Elves who keep it do not like visitors. The woollens are good and the cheese is better, but books must come all the way from Altdorf, and they cost accordingly."

A letter from [From.GetFirstName] in Marienburg:\n\n"There is no city like Marienburg. Ships from every shore crowd the harbour, the Burgomeisters answer to no Emperor, and the great temple of Manann, which all his temples obey, stands over the docks. The university was founded by merchants and its masters think like merchants. Every lecture has a price, and so does every book, every candle and every friend."

A letter from [From.GetFirstName] in Kufra:\n\n"The caravans come into Kufra out of the desert, and with them come scholars from every city of Araby. The masters teach the stars, the laws of the Sultans and the arts of numbers, and they dispute each other in the courtyards until the call to evening prayer. Water and paper are dear here, and a scholar is expected to pay well for both."
Found the University of Salzenmund
Salzenmund is a free town of learned men with no university to teach them. Pay for the halls and the first chairs, and the young nobles of the north will no longer have to go to Altdorf to study.
Found the University of Marienburg

The merchants of Marienburg have money, ships and the trade of the whole world, but no university. Pay for the halls and the first chairs, and the city will school the sons and daughters of the Wasteland and the north of the Empire.
The university is founded, a §YRector§! takes the chair and it begins to take students.
University of Sudenburg
To the University of Sudenburg.

A letter from [From.GetFirstName] in Sudenburg:\n\n"Sudenburg is the Empire at the edge of the world. The halls are new and smell of fresh timber, the masters are men who came south for gold or glory and stayed for the learning, and the jungle comes right up to the walls. We study the beasts and plants of the Southlands, the stars of the southern sky and the old ruins in the green. Everything must come by ship from the north, and everything costs three times what it would in Altdorf."
Found the University of Sudenburg

Sudenburg holds the Empire's banner far in the south, but its young nobles must sail half the world to study. Pay for the halls and the first chairs, and the Southlands will have a university of their own.
